newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus airline unit to transport steel tanks.
newsitem.headline: Airbus airline unit to transport steel tanks.

text.p: European aircraft manufacturer, Airbus Industrie said its airline subsidiary, Airbus Transport International (ATI), is to carry what is probably the most bulky air cargo ever transported.

ATI has signed a charter agreement to fly 18 special steel tanks between Clermont Ferrand, in central France and Le Havre over the next two to three years using its Super Transporter A300- 600ST(ST) "Beluga" freighters," an Airbus Industrie official told Reuters.

The tanks, each measuring just over 17 metres in length, 5.4 metres in diametre and weighing 39 tonnes, are being manufactured by a small French engineering company, the Societe Europeene de Chaudronnerie Industrielle (SECI), based some 60 kilometres south-east of Clermont Ferrand at Brioude.

"The contract with ATI entails 18 flights, one per tank, with the first scheduled for early May. Each tank is around 350 cubic metres in volume and probably represents the biggest shipment ever transported by air," said SECI's chairman and managing director, Paul Dugo.
The tanks are to be installed on a chemical ship now being fitted out at in Le Havre.

Dugo said moving the tanks by road would have been a laborious and costly exercise involving dismantling of telephone and power lines on certain stretches and also necessitating a special itinerary, taking six to seven days to complete, in order to avoid obstacles such as bridges.

"We compared this with the capabilites of Airbus' Super Transporter and the fact that by air, the 650 kilometres between Clermont Ferrand and Le Havre could be covered in around one hour and the choice was made.
There could be scope for further co-operation with ATI as SECI expanded its export business in Italy, Greece, the former Yugoslavia and Spain, Dugot added.
Airbus has two ST's currently in service and plans to take delivery of a third at the end of May 1997 and a fourth in 1998.

"The Super Transporter's (ST's) primary role is in transporting sections of Airbus aircraft from factories in Europe to final assembly lines in Toulouse and Hamburg. However, as the chemical tanks contract shows, we are also targeting ad hoc charters flights in utilising spare capacity," the Airbus official confirmed.

"While such charters will remain a sideline for us, we do see a niche market for outsize, high value cargoes such as satellites, the larger airliner engines, helicopters and other bulky loads. Our main competitor is probably the Antonov AN-124 which is tonnage rather than volume-orientated," the official added.

Airbus data shows that the ST is the world's largest cargo aircraft in terms of volume, with a cargo bay 7.1 metres in diameter and over 39 metres long. It can carry loads of up to 45 tonnes over a distance of 1,670 kilometres.

"Because of capacity constraints, our ad hoc charter activity will only really begin with the arrival of our third ST and we expect it to account for around 20 percent of global flying hours undertaken by the aircraft".

The ST is manufactured by the Special Aircraft Transport International Company (SATIC) a joint-venture company in which Airbus Industrie shareholders, Aerospatiale and Deutsche Aerospace , each have a 50 percent stake.
Other partners in the Airbus consortium are British Aerospace and Construcciones Aeronauticas of Spain.
